guidance.summary: Before someone is given an account or physical access that reaches CUI, you run a defined screening on them and record that it was done. NIST does not dictate the depth; you define the criteria - typically identity verification, employment and reference checks, a criminal background check, and confirmation of US-person status when export-controlled CUI is involved - and apply them consistently to employees, temps, contractors and MSP staff who get CUI access.
guidance.machine_shop_example: The shop's personnel security procedure requires, before CUI access is granted, an I-9 identity check, a third-party criminal background check, two reference checks, and verification of US-person status for anyone touching ITAR-marked jobs. HR records the completion date on the onboarding checklist and IT will not create the account until HR has signed that line. The MSP contract requires the MSP to background-check any technician assigned to the shop and to certify this annually, and the shop keeps the certification letter.
typical_evidence: Personnel screening policy or procedure defining the criteria and when re-screening occurs
Onboarding checklists showing screening completed before account creation, for a sample of recent hires
Background-check vendor invoices or completion notices (the results themselves can stay confidential)
US-person verification record for export-controlled work
MSP or contractor agreement clause requiring screening and the vendor's attestation
Account-creation tickets dated after the screening completion date
common_gaps: Accounts created on day one before any background check comes back
Screening applied to employees only, not to temps, interns, contract programmers or the MSP
No written criteria, so the assessor cannot tell what 'screened' means
The owner 'knows everyone' and nothing is documented
remediation_steps: Write the screening procedure: criteria (identity, background-check scope, references, US-person status where required), who performs it, and the rule that no CUI system or physical access is granted until it is complete.
Add a screening line with date and HR initials to the onboarding checklist and make IT's account-provisioning ticket depend on it.
Contract a background-check provider and run checks on all current CUI users who were never screened; record completion dates.
Extend the requirement to third parties: add a clause to the MSP and contractor agreements and collect annual attestations.
Define re-screening triggers (for example promotion to an administrator role, or every five years) and audit a sample of records annually.

guidance.summary: You need a written offboarding and role-change process, and proof you follow it. When someone leaves, their accounts are disabled, MFA tokens, keys and badges are returned, shared passwords they knew are changed, and their devices and CUI media are recovered - the same day for terminations. When someone changes roles, their access is adjusted to the new role and the old access removed rather than accumulating. The system has to stay protected both while the change is happening and afterward.
guidance.machine_shop_example: HR opens an offboarding ticket the moment a departure is known. IT disables the AD and Entra ID account and revokes MFA and VPN before the exit interview ends for involuntary terminations and by end of day for voluntary ones, changes the shared CNC-controller and Wi-Fi passwords the person knew, collects the laptop, badge, keys and any encrypted USB drives, and converts the mailbox to a shared mailbox for the manager. When the quality inspector moved into sales, IT removed her from the CUI-Engineering and Quality groups and added the Sales group the same day, and the transfer checklist shows both changes. A quarterly access review catches anything missed.
typical_evidence: Personnel action (offboarding and transfer) procedure with timelines and responsibilities for HR, managers, IT and the MSP
Completed offboarding checklists or tickets for recent departures showing account-disable time, MFA and VPN revocation, equipment return and shared-password changes
Transfer tickets showing security-group membership changes
AD or Entra ID export of disabled accounts with dates matching HR termination dates
Key, badge and asset return records
common_gaps: IT finds out about departures weeks later, and accounts of former employees are still enabled
Shared shop-floor logins and Wi-Fi keys never changed after someone leaves
Transfers keep all old permissions, so long-tenured staff can access everything
MSP or vendor accounts never removed when the technician leaves the MSP
remediation_steps: Write the procedure: HR notifies IT of every termination and transfer the same day; IT disables accounts and revokes MFA, VPN, remote access and cloud sessions within 24 hours (immediately for involuntary departures); managers collect devices, badges, keys and media; shared credentials the person knew are rotated.
Build offboarding and transfer checklists (ticket templates) that record timestamps and who did each step, and require the manager's sign-off.
Eliminate or inventory shared accounts (controllers, Wi-Fi, vendor portals) so rotation on departure is a known, short list.
For transfers, define access by role (security groups per department) and require removal of the old role's groups when the new role is added.
Run a quarterly review comparing HR's active roster against enabled accounts in AD or Entra ID, the file server, GCC High, VPN and the MSP's tools, and document the fixes.
Include the MSP: require notification and account removal when their staff assigned to the shop change.
